title: Tool Argument Synthesis — Adversarial Playbook & Sandbox
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook + scratch sandbox for an adversarial-style eval harness that synthesizes and mutates tool arguments to stress our function-calling and tool-selection layers during model onboarding. Goal is to create a compact, reusable prompt/testset generator and a short scoring rubric so we can catch regressions early (esp. after quantized model swaps / compilation changes).

Context / motivation:
- We keep seeing subtle regressions where the model picks the right tool but mangles arg formats (dates, phone numbers, nested JSON) or silently omits required fields.
- Current evals capture high-level accuracy but not edge-case argument fidelity across multi-step tool chains.
- Need lightweight adversarial scenarios that are: deterministic-ish (seeded), parameterizable (mutation intensity), and easy to run as part of the onboarding smoke.

Non-goal:
- This doc is not an exhaustive corpus of all user intents. It's a stress harness focused on argument synthesis, format preservation, and selection consistency across steps.

Design overview (rough):
1) Prompt seeds: curated small set of intent templates (10–15) covering common tool classes: calendar, search, DB query, calculator, http-call, file-op, and code-run.
2) Mutation engine: deterministic mutators that can be toggled: whitespace/noise, unicode homoglyphs, partial arg renaming, value format swaps (MM/DD vs DD-MM-YYYY), nested-keys flattening, extra irrelevant keys.
3) Multi-step chains: compose 2–4 step flows where intermediate outputs are passed to downstream tool calls (examples: parse invite -> call calendar.create -> call notify).
4) Scoring: two axes — selection accuracy (did model call the expected tool id) and arg fidelity (did the arguments match expected schema/values).

Prompt seeds (examples):
- Calendar booking: "Book meeting with Dr. Alvarez next Tues 3pm for 30 minutes. Use conference room B. Add agenda: project retro."
  - expected tool: calendar.create
  - canonical args: {"title":"Meeting: Dr. Alvarez","start":"2026-03-17T15:00:00-07:00","duration_minutes":30,"location":"Conf B","agenda":"project retro"}

- Web search + summarization: "Find the latest Redwood inference latency benchmark vs. comparator X, return top 2 links and 3-sentence summary each."
  - expected tool: search.query then summarizer.summarize

- DB read-modify-write: "Increase plan seats for org-id 4231 by 10% if trial_end > today."
  - expected tool sequence: db.read -> decision logic -> db.update

Mutation types (engine):
- Noise: random extra spaces, tab injections, trailing punctuation.
- Homoglyph: replace ASCII with visually similar unicode (o -> ο, a -> ɑ).
- Case-shift: camelCase -> SNAKE_CASE or mixed caps.
- Key aliasing: "start_time" -> "startTime" -> "startsAt" (aliases list configurable).
- Value format swap: ISO8601 <-> epoch <-> human text.
- Partial redaction: redact 1 char of phone/email.
- Extra-keys: add irrelevant keys like {"debug":true} or nested empty object.
- Flattening: {"meeting":{"start":"...","end":"..."}} -> {"meeting.start":"...","meeting.end":"..."}

Test-case example (full):
- seed id: CAL-001
- seed prompt: (see Calendar booking above)
- mutations: [Noise, Key aliasing(start_time->startTime), Value format swap(ISO->human)]
- expected tool: calendar.create
- expected args after canonicalization: title ~ contains "Dr. Alvarez"; start parseable to 2026-03-17T15:00-07:00; duration_minutes=30; location contiguous token includes "Conf B"
- tolerance: fuzzy-match on title (levenshtein <= 5), start parseable by dateutil, duration exact numeric match, location substring match
- scoring weight: selection 0.6, args 0.4

Multi-step flow example (chain):
- seed id: INV-007
- flow: user asks to schedule a prep meeting with a list of attendees pulled from CRM and to post summary to #eng Slack afterwards.
- step1: crm.lookup(org=redwood, role=pm) -> returns list of emails
- step2: calendar.create(start, attendees=list)
- step3: slack.post(channel="#eng-product", text=summary)
- adversarial mutation: crm returned display names with accented chars and one missing email; expect model to still call calendar.create with normalized emails only.
- checks: each step called in correct order; missing-field fallback handled (i.e. model asks clarifying question or uses fallback users); slack message contains event link if calendar API returned link.

Scoring rubric (proposal):
- Tool selection accuracy: 0/1 per expected tool call (1 if call matches expected tool identifier exactly; partial credit 0.5 if wrong version but compatible e.g., calendar.create.v1 vs calendar.create.v2 and schema compatible).
- Arg fidelity: per-field score 0..1; numeric exact match (1), parseable-with-transformation (0.75), semantically equivalent (0.5), incorrect/missing (0).
- Chain score: geometric mean across steps to penalize single-step failures.
- Overall pass: selection >= 0.9 and arg fidelity >= 0.85 for seeded run at mutation intensity low; for high intensity, track as degradation curve.

Automation notes (implementation sketch):
- Use the existing harness repo (linked) with a new runner: adversarial_runner.py that takes seed_file + mutation_profile + seed.
- Keep mutation engine deterministic when seeded. Make mutation profiles: low/medium/high.
- Output artifacts per run: structured logs (JSONL) of prompt_in, prompt_out, model_calls (tool id + args), canonical_expected, scoring_summary. These are what onboarding pipelines will compare across model versions.

Observability / regressions dashboard ideas:
- Small cards per seed showing trend lines (selection accuracy, arg fidelity) across model versions and compiler/quantization job ids.
- Highlight newly introduced failure modes (e.g., loss of iso-date parsing after kernel swap).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we allow the model to ask clarifying questions for missing args and treat those as correct behavior? (Pros: realistic; Cons: harder to score).
- Which schema canonicalizer do we use for arg equivalence? (dateutil + custom normalizers planned).
- Integration with rollout policy: threshold for automated canary failover? map scores to canary gate.
- Add negative tests for malicious args (command injection in code-run tool).

Immediate next steps (short checklist):
- [ ] Finalize seed list (assign owners): Maya -> calendar + slack seeds, Luca -> db + crm seeds, Priya -> http/code-run seeds.
- [ ] Implement mutation engine skeleton (low/med/high) and unit tests.
- [ ] Add CI job that runs adversarial harness on new model bundle PRs (proposal: run low-intensity suite). Link to PR template.
- [ ] Quick demo run across three recent model versions and capture baseline curves.

Quick notes / fragments from last pairing session:
- "flattening+aliasing combos were surprisingly destructive for the older 7B quantized builds"
- "When we pass extra irrelevant keys the newer runtime prunes them; older runtimes passed literal nulls — not consistent"
- Need to decide canonical naming for calendar location fields (room vs location vs venue).

References / links (working):
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ML-ONBOARD-ARG-SYNTH
- Existing harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/toolflow/tree/main/harness
- Related jira: JIRA-ML-1423 (seed collection + scoring)

Contact / owner notes:
- Rohan Mehta (owner for initial playbook) — ping me in #eng-applied-ml for pair sessions.

Appendix: short sample prompt bank (seeded):
- CAL-001, CAL-002 (back-to-back booking edgecases), INV-007 (crm chain), DB-INT-3 (null values in returns), HTTP-JSON-5 (malformed JSON bodies), CODE-RUN-2 (shell injection pattern), SEARCH-PRIO-1 (ambiguous comparator names).

End of draft.

Notes-to-self: keep this light — the canonical corpus will live in the repo and this doc is the design + tracker until we ship the first 200 seeds.
